UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA ALEXANDRIA DIVISION

MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,

Plaintiff,  v.  KATIE HALL, individually; NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN; META PLATFORMS, INC.; and JOHN/JANE DOES 1–6,

Defendants. ____________________________________/

Case No. 1:26-cv-02331

PLAINTIFF’S RULE 54(b) MOTION TO RECONSIDER ECF NO. 108 AS TO ECF NO. 103

Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine moves under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 54(b) for reconsideration of the Order signed and filed October 29, 2026 and entered on the docket October 30, 2026 (ECF No. 108), insofar as it denied Plaintiff’s Motion for Entry of a Scheduling Order and, as Necessary, an Initial Pretrial Conference (ECF No. 103). Magistrate Judge William E. Fitzpatrick entered ECF No. 108. This Motion asks the Magistrate Judge to reconsider that Order. The ground asserted is clear error causing manifest injustice. Carlson v. Boston Sci. Corp., 856 F.3d 320, 325 (4th Cir. 2017). Under Local Civil Rule 7(F)(1), a Memorandum in Support accompanies this Motion, with Proposed Order A and Proposed Order B.

I.	GROUNDS

1.	ECF No. 103 requested three forms of relief. First, entry of a scheduling order after the report or consultation Rule 16(b)(1) requires. ECF No. 103 ¶ 9, at 3. Second, if the complete scheduling order should await disposition of a pending matter, a determination whether an initial scheduling conference could proceed now to establish the remaining case-management steps. ECF No. 103 ¶ 10, at 3. Third, if either step was postponed, a statement of the good cause found under Rule 16(b)(2) and the date or event on which scheduling would next be addressed. ECF No. 103 ¶ 11, at 4. ECF No. 103 did not seek immediate interrogatory responses, document production, or depositions. ECF No. 103, Part II, at 3.

2.	The ordinary Rule 16(b)(2) date for the scheduling order was October 13, 2026, subject to a finding of good cause for delay. Defendant National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (“NCMEC”) was served July 31, 2026. ECF No. 3 at 2. NCMEC appeared August 12, 2026. ECF No. 10 at 1. Sixty days after August 12, 2026 was Sunday, October 11, 2026. Monday, October 12, 2026 was a legal holiday. The period ran to Tuesday, October 13, 2026. Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(1)(C), 6(a)(6)(A), 16(b)(2). The Memorandum sets out the computation.

3.	ECF No. 108 denied ECF No. 103 on the following stated ground: “Here, the record reflects that the District Judge has chosen to refrain from beginning any discovery until resolution of the pending motions to dismiss.” ECF No. 108 at 2. ECF No. 108 identified the initial-conference request. ECF No. 108 at 1. It denied that request through the same discovery-postponement rationale applied to the scheduling order. It did not separately explain that application. It contains no express finding under Rule 16(b)(2). Its reasons may be read as an implicit determination that good cause exists to delay the scheduling order. Plaintiff challenges whether those reasons support postponing the initial-conference alternative. ECF No. 108 identifies no order or instruction as the source of the decision it attributes to the District Judge.

4.	A decision to postpone discovery bears on whether the complete scheduling order should be entered now. Judicial consultation at a Rule 16(b) scheduling conference is not itself document production, deposition testimony, or an interrogatory response. Preparatory steps for that conference can affect disclosure and discovery timing. The Court can address those consequences expressly while deciding whether judicial scheduling should proceed. Fed. R. Civ. P. 16(b)(3)(B)(i)–(ii), 16(c)(2)(F). ECF No. 108 applied a rationale directed to discovery to withhold judicial consultation without addressing whether that consultation could proceed while discovery remained deferred. That application is the error asserted.

5.	The source and scope of the decision attributed to the District Judge bear on that application. The District Judge’s entries of record are ECF Nos. 12, 25, 48, 50, and 70. None addresses the Rule 16(b) schedule. Local Civil Rule 72 permits a magistrate judge to act on the instructions of a district judge. The local rule does not itself establish that such an instruction exists in this action or what it says. Plaintiff requests identification of any operative order or instruction to the extent necessary to determine the scheduling obligations in this action and the scope of the authority referred.

6.	Plaintiff requests correction of the disposition or, in the alternative, a stated basis and scope for its continuation and a defined next step. Neither form of relief compels immediate merits discovery. Rule 54(b) permits revision of ECF No. 108 at any time before final judgment. ECF No. 108 was entered Friday, October 30, 2026. This Motion is submitted Sunday, November 1, 2026.

II.	SCOPE

7.	This Motion concerns only the denial of ECF No. 103. It does not seek reconsideration of the denial of ECF No. 105. It does not renew the requests denied in ECF No. 84. It does not seek authorization of interrogatories, document requests, depositions, or any other discovery. It does not seek a determination concerning the successor designation. Plaintiff’s pending applications remain pending on their own terms. None is withdrawn or expanded by this Motion. This Motion does not replace any separate objection required to obtain review of ECF No. 108.

III.	RELIEF REQUESTED

8.	Plaintiff requests that the Court:

(a)	reconsider ECF No. 108 insofar as it denied ECF No. 103, and modify that disposition;

(b)	establish a Rule 16(b) scheduling procedure for this action;

(c)	set a scheduling conference under Rule 16(b)(1)(B) and Local Civil Rule 16(B) on a date certain within 21 days after entry of the order, unless a sufficient Rule 26(f) report filed before that date permits earlier entry of the scheduling order without a conference;

(d)	direct the parties’ preparatory conference and written report on calendar dates fixed by the Court, each falling after entry of the order, with the intervals shortened under Rules 26(f)(1) and 26(f)(4) and Local Civil Rule 26(A)(1) as requested in ECF No. 103 ¶ 9(c), at 3, and provide that a qualifying conference and report already completed satisfy that direction;

(e)	hold the initial conference and establish the remaining case-management steps even if the Court determines that completion of the scheduling order should await disposition of the pending motions to dismiss; and

(f)	in the alternative, if the Court continues to postpone both the scheduling order and the initial conference, identify any operative order or instruction on which the postponement rests and its application to each of those steps; state the Court’s basis for the continued postponement under Rule 16(b)(2); and establish a procedure under which the Court will take the next scheduling step within 14 days after disposition of the last pending motion to dismiss, if the action remains pending, with authority to proceed earlier where an individual disposition permits.

9.	The 21-day, seven-day, three-day, and 14-day periods are requested case-management terms. The rules do not impose them. The alternative request in paragraph 8(f) is not consent to postponement. ECF No. 103 ¶ 12, at 4.

10.	Proposed Order A and Proposed Order B are submitted with this Motion. Plaintiff relies on the existing record.

Marvelle J. Ballentine

Plaintiff, pro se
